inheritedFrom: LLP 0102 cross-application acceptance kernel, via LLP 0137's contract lineage and evidence conventions
everyArmRetains: at least two named authenticated actors plus an outsider
one actor-specific positive transition and one cross-user negative
authoritative data observed independently of the initiating UI
realtime transport attribution: push, poll, local optimistic state, or unsupported
operation settlement, including retry or ambiguity where applicable
expected check count, so a vacuous pass fails
command exit status and structured failure classification
exact package versions the arm ran against
assistance events and external-consumer posture breaks
what Snapback did better than the reference evidence and what must not regress
nonEvidence: A rendered update alone does not prove backend state, push delivery, auth, or settlement.
Polling does not count as native push.
Optimistic UI does not count as authority.
A cached seed does not count as an offline mutation.
Client animation does not count as authoritative streaming.
Seeded state does not prove a mutation.
A rendered Expo screen does not count as an OS lifecycle proof.
stopRule: Any cross-user data disclosure, secret exposure, destructive cleanup against an unrelated target, false capability claim, or late effect after a confirmed cancellation is a Stop-class defect. Metric work pauses until the defect is understood. Failed attempts, security Stops, credential incidents, and builder mistakes are preserved with correct attribution.
performanceRule: Performance observations follow LLP 0035 and support only the workload actually measured.
